title: 🔍 A Russian Spy Tracks Employees of a US Tech Company — and Photographs Their Screens in a Café!
body: 🔍 A Russian Spy Tracks Employees of a US Tech Company — and Photographs Their Screens in a Café!

A US federal grand jury has charged a 25-year-old Russian citizen with acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice, and spying on employees of a major Silicon Valley tech and defense company, in a case announced on November 18. The charges also include interstate stalking and identity-document forgery.

According to the indictment, the young man was recruited via the "Telegram" app, and entered the United States illegally in the summer of 2026 after a journey from Istanbul to Mexico City and then across the border. His handlers tasked him with buying computers, phones, wireless network equipment, and remote-access software, then sitting in a café near the company's office in Palo Alto to photograph employees' computer screens while they worked, and placing his computer in specific spots so the handlers could access it remotely and collect data from nearby employees. The company is targeted — according to the charges — because it supplies Ukraine with technologies used in its war with Russia; the official statement did not name the company, but press reports said it is "Palantir".

On September 3, the defendant followed a female employee for about 50 kilometers from Palo Alto toward San Francisco, despite her attempts to shake him off with turns and back roads — he even ran a red light to keep following her — until she called emergency services and drove to a police station. Investigators found in his home about $18,000 in cash, two computers, two phones, two Russian passports, and forged documents, including a California ID card, an altered US passport, and a Social Security card under a pseudonym, plus a notebook with 10 handwritten addresses and detailed files on at least three employees. He was arrested on October 30, appears in court again on November 24, and faces up to 21 years in prison if convicted on all four charges.
Simply put: an unregistered foreign agent is a person secretly working for another government inside a country without informing its authorities — a crime separate from espionage itself.
Did you imagine that spying on tech companies happens this way, in cafés?
